answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make each identity cost real money to fake. Every agent locks a bond before it can grade peers, and a bad attestation burns part of that bond. Spinning up a crowd of fake agents then means locking funds for each one, so the attack cost scales with its size. Reputation also has to be earned slowly, so a jade-level score only comes from honest work over time, while a hollow account with no history carries almost no weight in grading. A ridge of stake and history keeps the network honest.
